title: Myotomes & Key Muscles
summary: Screen every root from C1 to S2 with one movement each, know the ISNCSCI key muscles, and combine myotome, dermatome and reflex to name the level.
ur: Har root (C1 se S2) ki ek movement test karna, ISNCSCI key muscles yaad rakhna aur dermatome + reflex ke saath level pehchaanna.

sources.title: ASIA — ISNCSCI (2019 revision)
sources.note: Key muscles and motor scoring, ASIA Impairment Scale.

goals.beginner: Name the movement for every myotome from C1 to S2.
goals.intermediate: Test each myotome correctly and know the ISNCSCI key muscles.
goals.advanced: Combine myotome, dermatome and reflex to localise a root.
goals.expert: Separate root, nerve and cord lesions; classify spinal cord injury.

concepts.title: What is a myotome?
concepts.body: A **myotome** is the group of muscles supplied by **one spinal nerve root**. Most muscles get fibres from two or three roots, so a single root lesion causes **weakness**, not paralysis.
concepts.ur: Myotome = ek root ke muscles. Ek root kharab ho to kamzori aati hai, mukammal paralysis nahi.

concepts.title: The screen in one table
concepts.body: Learn the movements in order — say them out loud from the neck to the foot.

concepts.title: How to screen
concepts.body: Myotomes are tested as **resisted isometric holds** in mid-range: “Hold — don't let me move you” for about **5 seconds**. Compare both sides, and repeat if you suspect fatigue (a root lesion often weakens after a few repetitions).

concepts.title: ISNCSCI key muscles
concepts.body: For spinal cord injury the international standard grades **10 key muscles** per side (0–5, supine): C5 elbow flexors, C6 wrist extensors, C7 elbow extensors, C8 finger flexors, T1 little-finger abductors, L2 hip flexors, L3 knee extensors, L4 ankle dorsiflexors, L5 long toe extensors, S1 ankle plantarflexors.
concepts.ur: Spinal cord injury mein har side ke 10 key muscles ko 0–5 grade kiya jaata hai.

concepts.title: Pitfalls
concepts.body: Pain inhibits muscles — a painful knee will 'test weak' for L3. Large muscles (quadriceps, calf) are hard to break manually: use functional tests (single-leg squat, heel and toe walking, heel raises). Always compare with the other side.

concepts.title: Localise with the triad
concepts.body: A root lesion shows up in **myotome + dermatome + reflex** together. Two out of three matching the same level is convincing.

concepts.title: Which disc hits which root?
concepts.body: In the **cervical** spine the root exits **above** its vertebra: a C5–C6 disc affects the **C6** root. In the **lumbar** spine a posterolateral disc affects the **traversing** root: an L4–L5 disc affects **L5**, an L5–S1 disc affects **S1**. A far-lateral disc can hit the exiting root instead.

concepts.title: Root or peripheral nerve?
concepts.body: Test muscles that share a **root** but not a **nerve**. Foot drop with weak hip abduction (superior gluteal) and inversion (tibial) = L5 root. Foot drop with normal hip abduction and inversion = common fibular nerve. Wrist drop with weak elbow extension = high radial nerve or C7; with normal triceps = radial nerve at the spiral groove.

concepts.title: ASIA Impairment Scale (AIS)
concepts.body: After grading key muscles and sensation, classify the spinal cord injury.

head: Grade
Meaning
rows: No sensory or motor function in S4–S5
Sensation (not motor) preserved below the level including S4–S5; no motor function more than 3 levels below the motor level on either side
Motor function preserved below the level; more than half of key muscles below the neurological level have grade < 3
At least half of key muscles below the neurological level have grade ≥ 3
Sensation and motor function normal in a person who had prior deficits

questions.prompt: Great toe extension tests which myotome?
questions.explain: EHL = L5.

questions.prompt: Elbow extension is mainly…
questions.explain: Triceps = C7.

questions.prompt: Which movement screens L3?
questions.explain: Quadriceps = L3 (L2–L4).

questions.prompt: Finger abduction screens…
questions.explain: Interossei/ADM = T1.

questions.prompt: Why does a single root lesion cause weakness rather than paralysis?
options: Most muscles receive fibres from more than one root
questions.explain: Overlap between roots preserves partial function.

questions.prompt: The ISNCSCI key muscle for C6 is…
questions.explain: C6 = wrist extensors (ECRL/ECRB).

questions.prompt: How long should a myotome isometric hold last?
questions.explain: A 5-second hold reveals weakness and early fatigue.

questions.prompt: The best way to detect mild S1 weakness is…
questions.explain: The calf is too strong to break manually — functional repetition detects weakness.

questions.prompt: How many key muscles per side does ISNCSCI grade?
questions.explain: 5 upper-limb + 5 lower-limb key muscles per side.

questions.prompt: A C5–C6 cervical disc usually affects which root?
questions.explain: Cervical roots exit above their vertebra: C5–C6 disc → C6 root.

questions.prompt: A posterolateral L4–L5 disc usually affects…
questions.explain: The traversing root (L5) is compressed.

questions.prompt: Weak wrist extension, numb thumb, reduced brachioradialis reflex =
questions.explain: All three point to C6.

questions.prompt: Which reflex matches the L5 myotome?
questions.explain: L5 = medial hamstring reflex.

questions.case: Foot drop after a fibular-neck fracture. Hip abduction 5/5, inversion 5/5, eversion 2/5.
questions.prompt: Lesion?
questions.explain: Normal hip abduction and inversion exclude L5; eversion + dorsiflexion = common fibular.

questions.case: SCI: no sensation or movement in S4–S5.
questions.prompt: AIS grade?
questions.explain: No sacral sparing = complete (AIS A).

questions.case: SCI at T10: perianal sensation present; no voluntary movement below the level.
questions.prompt: AIS grade?
questions.explain: Sensory but not motor sparing below the level including S4–S5 = AIS B.

questions.case: SCI: below the neurological level, 4 of 6 key muscles are grade 3 or more.
questions.prompt: AIS grade?
questions.explain: At least half the key muscles below the level ≥ 3 = AIS D.

questions.case: Bilateral hand weakness and clumsiness, brisk leg reflexes and a positive Hoffmann sign.
questions.prompt: Think first of…
questions.explain: Upper motor neuron signs below the level point to the cord, not the roots.

questions.case: Weak ankle plantarflexion (can't do 10 heel raises), weak great toe flexion, absent Achilles reflex, numb lateral foot.
questions.prompt: Most likely level?
options: Tibial nerve at the tarsal tunnel
questions.explain: Plantarflexion + Achilles reflex + lateral foot = S1.

questions.case: Weak shoulder abduction and elbow flexion, numb lateral arm, biceps reflex reduced; neck pain after a fall.
questions.prompt: Most likely level?
questions.explain: Two different nerves (axillary + musculocutaneous) affected together = their shared root, C5.

questions.case: An athlete's arm hangs weak for a few minutes after a tackle with burning down the arm, then recovers fully.
questions.prompt: Best explanation?
options: Transient brachial plexus/root traction injury ('burner/stinger') — screen myotomes before return to play
questions.explain: Unilateral and transient = burner; bilateral symptoms would demand cord assessment.

questions.prompt: Why must a myotome be tested with a sustained hold of about 5 seconds?
options: Mild root weakness often shows only as fatigue under a sustained load
questions.explain: A brief push can hide early weakness; a sustained isometric hold reveals it.

stations.title: Upper-limb myotome screen
stations.scenario: Screen myotomes C5–T1 on both sides in a patient with neck and arm pain.
tasks: Test each myotome isometrically for 5 seconds.
checklist: C6 elbow flexion and wrist extension
C7 elbow extension and wrist flexion
Holds about 5 seconds and compares sides
Links weakness to the matching dermatome and reflex

stations.title: Lower-limb myotome screen
stations.scenario: Screen myotomes L2–S2 in a patient with sciatica.
checklist: S1 plantarflexion (single-leg heel raises) and eversion
Compares sides and reports the level
